note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Severe left-sided headache since early morning, woke patient at approx. 5:30 am (earlier than usual 7:00 am wake time), still present at time of consult.
- History: Previous headaches, but less severe and typically distributed across the front of the head; this episode is notably more severe and localized to the left side. No previous similar one-sided headaches.
- Associated symptoms: Mild photophobia (eye soreness with bright lights, tolerable), transient dizziness on waking (subsided), no neck stiffness, no fever, no significant nausea, headache may feel sore initially when lying down but improves with rest.
- Exacerbating factors: Work-related stress ongoing for ~2 months, including late nights and backlog of work.
- Mood: Some frustration, occasional anxiety, but no anger or mood disorder reported; mood "ebbs and flows."
- No family history of migraine. Family history of anxiety (mother).
- Past medical history: Anxiety (~2 years).
- Medications: Sertraline (dose/route/frequency not documented), Paracetamol (taken this morning, dose/route/frequency not documented; not effective).
- Allergies: None known.
- Social history: Lives with partner, non-smoker, has a cat, runs three times a week, diet "OK," no recreational drug use documented.

Objective:
- No examination (telephone consult; unable to examine).
- No documented vital signs.
- No investigation results available.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Headache (acute, severe, left-sided)
   - Assessment: Likely tension headache vs. migraine (differential considered: features of stress, anxiety support tension headache; one-sided pain and photophobia suggest migraine).
   - Differential diagnosis: Migraine, tension-type headache.
   - Investigations planned: None at this time; consider blood tests if no improvement or if symptoms worsen at follow-up.
   - Treatment planned: Start Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented). Continue Paracetamol if desired. Recommended hydration (1.5-2 L fluids daily, excluding caffeinated drinks), adequate sleep (7-8 hours/night), and rest. Advise time off work if possible to reduce stress.
   - Relevant referrals: Provide link to local self-referral counseling service for stress management. Review in 1 week (follow-up appointment planned). Provide patient information on headache red flags/danger signs.

2. Work-related stress/anxiety
   - Assessment: Ongoing work-related stress and history of anxiety; currently stable, no self-harm ideation.
   - Treatment planned: Recommend exploring counseling services for support.
   - Relevant referrals: Counseling service referral (self-referral link to be provided).

Quality checks:
●	Missing clinically expected elements: No physical examination or vital signs documented. Sertraline dose/route/frequency not documented. No specific dose for Paracetamol or Ibuprofen noted. Detailed headache character (e.g., pulsating, pressure), duration per episode not specifically described beyond onset.
●	Internal conflicts: None noted.
●	Transcript quality: Good; audio appears clear and responses well documented.
